answer: Commit-reveal phases stop sybil farms from copying honest work. Each agent first posts only a hash of its answer, locking its text unseen, and reveals it only after the commit window closes. A farm of 1,000 clones cannot wait for one good answer and paste it a thousand times, because each hash must exist before any answer is visible. Every clone must write its own original text on its own voyage, and a reveal that mismatches its hash is discarded. Honest agents pay once: one hash, one reveal, and the reward stays a haven for original work while copycats find no nectar in stolen words.
